meta_analysis: Ng et al. (2023) — MASEM of mediators of CBT/IPT for youth depression
rationale: Schema covers 5 variables (IPT, male_pct, dxgive, Source, MedCat). For multi-label fields (Source, MedCat) we extract at the measure level and aggregate to a study-level set. The mediator-instrument lookup skill (rules/ng_mediator_lookup) is the main leverage rule for MedCat accuracy.

fields.name: Sample
fields.definition: Total participants randomized in this study record. The sample_key is a GENERIC within-paper label — 'main sample' for most papers; 'CBT arm' and 'IPT arm' for the dual-arm CBT+IPT exception. DO NOT include the paper's author or year in the sample_key. This field anchors the within-paper sample census; the per-record IPT / male_pct / dxgive / Source / MedCat values key off the same labels.

fields.name: IPT
fields.definition: Therapy approach tested in this study. 0 = CBT (cognitive, cognitive-behavioral, problem-solving training, rational-emotive, restructuring/reframing, self-control training, verbal self-instructional training). 1 = IPT (Interpersonal Psychotherapy, including IPT-A, IPT-AST variants). DUAL-ARM EXCEPTION: a paper that tests BOTH a CBT arm and an IPT arm in the same RCT contributes TWO study records keyed 'CBT arm' and 'IPT arm'; all other fields (male_pct, dxgive, Source, MedCat) are shared between the two records.
fields.skill_hints: Look at Methods → 'Treatment'/'Intervention' section. Treatment name 'IPT' or 'interpersonal psychotherapy' or 'IPT-A' or 'IPT-AST' → 1. Otherwise (CBT, problem-solving training, behavioral activation, etc.) → 0.

fields.name: male_pct
fields.comment_on_gender: IS the gender metric, NOT decomposed [total, female, male]. female_pct = 100 - male_pct is trivially derivable.
fields.definition: Percentage of the sample that is male, rounded to 2 decimal places (e.g., 66.67%). If only N_male and N_total are reported, compute (N_male / N_total) × 100. If only verbal descriptors are given, follow codebook defaults: Marginal/Few = 15%, Some = 30%, Majority = 60%, Mainly/Predominantly/Primarily = 90%.
fields.skill_hints: Find the Participants/Sample description in Methods. Prefer randomized-sample %male over enrolled or screened. For all-female samples emit 0; for all-male emit 100.

fields.name: dxgive

value_labels.110: Yes, ALL of sample met diagnostic criteria for a depressive disorder
value_labels.120: Yes, SOME portion of sample met diagnostic criteria
value_labels.200: NONE of sample met diagnostic criteria (e.g., prevention trial that excluded diagnosed)
value_labels.400: Diagnosis NOT assessed, mentioned, or reported

fields.definition: Whether participants met formal diagnostic criteria for a depressive disorder (MDD, persistent depressive disorder/dysthymia, minor depressive disorder, or depressive disorder NOS). 3-digit categorical code where leading digit encodes top-level: 1=Yes, 2=No, 4=Unknown.
fields.skill_hints: Read Methods → Eligibility/Inclusion Criteria. 'Met DSM-IV/5 criteria for MDD' as required → 110. 'Eligible if elevated symptoms; some met dx' → 120. 'Excluded if diagnosed' (typical prevention trial) → 200. No mention of diagnosis at all → 400.

fields.name: Source

value_labels.5: Teacher (or teacher-like adult: counselor, milieu worker, probation officer)
value_labels.7: Researcher (RA, independent evaluator, clinician-rater; performance-based measures; interview-based judgments like K-SADS, CGI, GAF)
value_labels.8: Life-event data (external records: arrests, attendance, grades, urinalysis)
value_labels.9: Unknown (not reported and authors did not reply)

fields.definition: Rater/informant types used across all measures in the study. Multi-label: extract every distinct rater type for any measure (mediator or outcome). Emit as a SET of integers.
fields.skill_hints: For each measure in Methods, identify who completed it. 'Children/adolescents/youth completed the [scale]' → 1. 'Parent/mother/father completed' → 2. 'Teacher rated' → 5. 'Trained interviewer / clinician administered K-SADS / CGI / CDRS-R / HRSD' → 7. Per codebook rule: 'when there are multiple sources for one measure, code the smallest number'.
fields.comment: Codes 3, 4, 6, 8 are codebook-defined but rarely appear in youth-depression trials (sibling/peer/therapist/life-event sources are unusual for these measures). Schema accepts them but marks them low-prior.

fields.name: MedCat

value_labels.1: Negative cognition (a) — cognitive distortions, dysfunctional attitudes, hopelessness, low self-esteem, rumination, pessimistic attribution
value_labels.2: Pleasant activities (b) — activity scheduling, hobbies, behavioral activation, relaxation (NOT social)
value_labels.3: Problem solving (c) — primary control coping, active coping, generating solutions, conflict resolution
value_labels.4: Reframing (d) — secondary control coping, cognitive restructuring, distraction, acceptance, finding the silver lining
value_labels.5: Social engagement (e) — social skills, social support, prosocial behavior, loneliness, peer/dating quality
value_labels.l2: Family functioning (L2) — family dysfunction, expressed emotion, parent-youth conflict, cohesion, communication problems
value_labels.l29: Avoidance (L29) — avoidant coping, wishful thinking, denial

fields.definition: Mediator category for every measure in the study. Multi-label: emit a SET of distinct MedCat codes covering all measures. Codes 1-5 are the canonical 'high-priority' mediators (CMH a-e); 'l2' and 'l29' are 'low-priority' but central to this MA's IPT pathway; '99' marks depression-symptom outcome measures.
fields.skill_hints: For each measure, look up its name in the mediator_instruments.yaml table. Codebook rule (p. 11): 'prioritize the contents of the measure over the title'. If a measure has 2/3 items in social and 1/3 in family, code as social engagement (5). Code 99 for depression symptom outcomes only (BDI, CDI, CES-D, KSADS-depression-severity).
fields.validator_note: Compare schema output set with d_long gold set via Jaccard ≥ 0.66. Outcome code 99 is OPTIONAL — if gold has only mediator codes, drop 99 from schema before comparing.
